title: Music and Dance
subtitle: Rhythm as a form of memory
body: Music and dance sit at the heart of Murle community life, present at celebrations, age-set ceremonies, and everyday gatherings alike. Drums, chants, and call-and-response singing bring communities together across generations.

Dances are often tied to specific occasions — some celebrate a successful harvest or cattle raid recovery, others mark rites of passage. Movements and songs are learned informally by watching and joining in, rather than through formal instruction.
Many songs also serve as oral history, encoding stories of migration, notable leaders, or moral lessons into memorable rhythms that are easy to pass down.
This section will feature more detailed descriptions of specific songs and dances as they are documented with community members.
